title: Efficient Double-Length Tweakable Blockcipher Beating the Strong-PRP Bound
summary: One double-length construction merely meets the strong-PRP bound, while a bound-beating result has substantial performance cost; an efficient improvement remains open.

formal_statement.body: Construct an efficient $n$-bit-blockcipher-based tweakable blockcipher with $N=2n$ whose strong-PRP advantage beats $O(q^3/2^{2n})$.

scope.domain: Design of efficient expanding tweakable blockciphers from fixed-block-length blockciphers under strong-PRP security.
parameters: n: block length in bits of the underlying blockcipher
N: block length in bits of the tweakable blockcipher, constrained to twice n
q: variable governing the stated strong-PRP advantage bound
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct an efficient double-length tweakable blockcipher from an n-bit blockcipher whose strong-PRP advantage is asymptotically below order q cubed divided by 2 to the power 2n.

citations.label: A Modular Framework for Building Variable-Input-Length Tweakable Ciphers

progress.summary: The source reports no known efficient construction from an n-bit blockcipher that improves the stated strong-PRP bound. It contrasts a bound-beating result with substantial performance cost against a double-length construction that only meets the bound.
citation_labels: Thomas Shrimpton et al., A Modular Framework for Building Variable-Input-Length Tweakable Ciphers
